Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick onboarding help so far. Attached is PO_8234 for a mixed order placed by our Stockholm branch (GlobalRetail AB). The order contains:

- Platform subscription (monthly SaaS) — billed to GlobalRetail AB, customer VAT ID included in header of PO.
- Hardware: 15x barcode scanners (shipped to our Stockholm warehouse).

Can you confirm how Redwood will treat VAT for the two line items? Our expectation is: if the SaaS line is B2B and the VAT ID validates, it should be reverse-charged (0% on vendor invoice) and accounted by us in Sweden. The hardware line should carry Swedish VAT (25%) because it is a tangible good delivered in Sweden.

Two asks:
1) Please validate the VAT ID we sent and confirm whether you will apply reverse-charge on the SaaS line.
2) If possible, issue either a single invoice with explicit line-item tax amounts (service: 0% reverse-charge with VAT ID noted; goods: 25% VAT) or two separate invoices (service invoice + goods invoice). Our AP needs clear line-level tax for automated matching.

I've attached the PO and the customer's VAT registration page export. If you need a signed self-billing agreement to accept a single combined invoice, let me know and I can sign.

Attachments: [Attachment: PO_8234.pdf (pdf)] [Attachment: VAT_Certificate_GlobalRetail_2026.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks — can you confirm ETA for the corrected invoice?

Best,

Quick read: this is a fairly common mixed-supply case but a couple of checks first —

1) VAT ID validation: run the supplied VAT ID against VIES and keep the timestamped result in the billing record. The attached VAT certificate is helpful but VIES is canonical for us. If VIES returns valid and the VAT number matches the customer name/address, we can treat the SaaS line as B2B intra-EC supply and apply reverse-charge (0% on Redwood invoice).

2) Shipping proof: for the hardware line we need shipping/fulfilment evidence showing delivery in Sweden (tracking + delivery note). That supports charging Swedish VAT.

3) Invoicing approach: Billing Ops can either:
   a) Issue two invoices (service invoice with 0% reverse-charge; goods invoice with 25% VAT), or
   b) Issue a combined invoice with two clearly separated line items and explicit tax calculation per line + a note that the service line is reverse-charged under Art. 44/196 of the EU VAT Directive (or UK equivalent if later).

From a systems perspective, option (a) is simpler for AP matching; option (b) is acceptable if we capture: VIES validation screenshot, link to self-billing consent (if used), and the shipping proof in the invoice notes/attachments.

I've uploaded the internal tax matrix that maps GL codes and revenue recognition for mixed orders — Billing Ops should reference this.

ETA: If customer provides VAT cert + shipping proof today, Billing Ops can produce invoices within 48 business hours. Without docs expect 3–5 business days while we chase evidence.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bTaxMatrix [Attachment: internal-tax-matrix.pdf (pdf)]

— Ben

Adding operational steps so we have a clear playbook:

1) Validate VAT ID: Billing Ops to run VIES check and save the PDF screenshot into the billing record (field: vat_validation_doc). If VIES shows temporary downtime, accept the submitted VAT certificate + business registry extract for now but flag for follow-up.

2) Request shipping proof from customer (tracking + delivery note). Billing Ops to wait for proof before applying Swedish VAT to the goods line. If shipping proof not available, we may need to invoice at 25% and then credit back upon receipt.

3) Invoice creation: use two separate invoices for clarity —
   - Invoice S-8234: Services (monthly platform), net value, VAT 0% (reverse-charge). Note: include "Customer VAT ID: SE999999999" and reference to VIES check. GL code: REV-SaaS-10.
   - Invoice G-8234: Goods (barcode scanners), net value + 25% Swedish VAT. GL code: REV-Goods-40.

4) Self-billing: I prepared a DocuSign self-billing consent for GlobalRetail. If they sign, Billing Ops can attach the DocuSign envelope to the invoice and include a single combined invoice reference in our AP notes, but Ops should still create the two accounting invoices behind the scenes. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/recipient?doc=SB-8242 [Attachment: self-billing-docusign-link.txt]

5) ETA: with VAT cert + shipping proof we can deliver both invoices in ~48 hours (business). If customer signs self-billing it reduces AP back-and-forth for future orders.

Billing Ops — please pick this up and coordinate the invoice numbers with Finance.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations — Redwood Inference
